title: Find Unclaimed Money In Three Steps

beats.say: One in seven people has unclaimed money waiting, and you can check yours in three steps.
beats.visual: one lone brown suitcase circling on an empty airport baggage carousel under strip lights, overhead view, no people

beats.say: When a bank, employer or utility cannot reach you, the leftover money goes to the state.
beats.visual: a domed state capitol building glowing in golden hour light, seen across a sprinkler-wet lawn, long lens compression, no people

beats.say: Step one. Search your state's unclaimed property office through unclaimed dot org.
beats.visual: a pulled-out library card catalog drawer packed with index cards, macro with razor focus on the front edge, no people

beats.say: Searching costs nothing, and the government will not call or text asking for a fee.
beats.visual: a glass phone booth glowing yellow in a snowy empty lot with the receiver left dangling, low angle wide shot, no people

beats.say: Step two. Repeat the search in every other state where you have lived.
beats.visual: aerial view of square farm fields cut by dirt roads forking toward three tiny towns, extreme wide, no people

beats.say: MissingMoney dot com, sponsored by state officials, checks most states at once.
beats.visual: an old telephone switchboard wall of patch cables with a few small bulbs lighting at once, eye level close-up, no people

beats.say: Step three. When you find a match, file a claim with the state office that holds it.
beats.visual: a rubber date stamp and a red ink pad on a blank form, overhead flat-lay, no readable text, no people

beats.say: Expect to prove it is yours, but claims cost nothing, and state treasurers say the right never expires.
beats.visual: a giant tortoise plodding across a sunny dirt path, low angle from ground level, no people

beats.say: Here is the part nobody tells you. Money can sit under an old name or a misspelling, so try variations.
beats.visual: a worn-smooth metal nameplate screwed beside an old brick doorway with the letters rubbed away, macro, no people

beats.say: The honest catch: you may find nothing, and scammers pose as officials, so use only official state sites.
beats.visual: a feathered fishing lure hanging above dark still river water with its reflection, eye level, bright midday glare, no people

beats.say: If anyone pushes a fee or a rush, stop and search the state site yourself.
beats.visual: a striped railway crossing gate lowered across empty tracks, twin red lamps glowing, silhouette against an orange dusk sky, no people

beats.say: This is education, not advice. Check your state's site for current steps and documents.
beats.visual: an empty porch swing swaying slightly beside a screen door in late afternoon light, medium shot, no people

beats.say: Follow for the money rules school never taught you.
beats.visual: a paper kite rising into a pale morning sky above a wheat field, wide shot, no people

description: About one in seven people has unclaimed property waiting, according to state treasurers and NAUPA. Search your state at unclaimed.org, repeat in every state where you have lived, then file a claim with the state office that holds the money. Searching and claiming cost nothing, and officials will not call or text asking for a fee. Educational only, not financial advice.
first_comment: Have you ever searched for unclaimed money in your name? Educational only, not financial advice.

facts.claim: Every state has a free process to search for unclaimed funds, found through unclaimed.org/search; the government will not call or text and ask you to pay to search
facts.basis: FTC Consumer Alert, How to handle unexpected calls about unclaimed funds, 2026-03-30 (consumer.ftc.gov)

facts.claim: If you have lived in other states, check their unclaimed property offices too
facts.basis: USA.gov, How to find unclaimed money from the government (usa.gov/unclaimed-money); NAUPA unclaimed.org/search says to check each state you have lived or done business in

facts.claim: MissingMoney.com is the free multi-state search sponsored by NAUPA and endorsed by the states; there is no fee to search; 1 in 7 individuals have unclaimed property waiting; owners can reclaim in perpetuity; unclaimed property includes inactive accounts, missed paychecks and utility refunds
facts.basis: NAST and NAUPA statement on the MissingMoney.com relaunch (unclaimed.org/nast-and-naupa-relaunch-missingmoney-com)

facts.claim: Claims are processed at no cost, and the claimant must provide documentation to establish ownership; try name variations, nicknames, misspellings and previous addresses when searching
facts.basis: Missouri State Treasurer Unclaimed Property FAQ (treasurer.mo.gov); NY State Comptroller how to search and claim (osc.ny.gov); NAUPA unclaimed.org/search

facts.claim: Scammers posing as government officials use fake agency names, pressure to act fast and upfront processing fees; the safe move is to search your state's official site yourself
facts.basis: FTC Consumer Alert, How to handle unexpected calls about unclaimed funds, 2026-03-30 (consumer.ftc.gov)
